text:
lana: Quick sync — product needs a decision on inference perf priorities for next quarter. We have limited eng runway and three competing asks: improve 95th latency (hotpath), increase throughput for batched workloads, and cut per-token cost for high-volume customers. Thoughts on framework?

matt: We should do RICE-ish but split by workload slice. Hotpath/chat users = high impact on conversion; batch/embeds = high reach but lower urgency.

olivia: Data: last 30 days, 95th latency breaches up 18% for chat customers after deploys; embeddings QPS steady but cost spike is top complaint from acme corp. I can attach logs if needed.

ravi: Practical constraints: Dedicated capacity footprint + GPU queuing means throughput improvements need infra changes (pool autoscale tweak + batching logic). Latency wins can come from KV-cache and shorter scheduling path — smaller scope.

lana: Proposed approach: score each initiative with R/I/C/E where Impact = product/ARR/ops risk, Reach = % of calls, Confidence = data+POC, Effort = eng+infra weeks. Then map to short (1 sprint), med (2-4), long (quarter+).

matt: Example quick RICE notes:
```
Improve 95p latency (chat hotpath): R 8, I 7, C 0.8, E 3 -> RICE = (8*7*0.8)/3 = 14.93
Throughput (batch QPS): R 9, I 5, C 0.7, E 6 -> RICE = (9*5*0.7)/6 = 5.25
Cost optim (quant+cache): R 7, I 9, C 0.6, E 5 -> RICE = (7*9*0.6)/5 = 7.56
```

olivia: Those numbers feel right directionally. Suggest we separate short-term latency quick wins (cache TTLs, scheduler) from larger infra batching changes. Short wins unblock customer SLAs faster.

ravi: Agree. Also add sequencing dependency: we can do cache+scheduler now, but if we later change batching kernel selection that may invalidate some perf assumptions. So add "dependency risk" as a qualifier.

lana: Good call. For launch criteria: define SLO delta (95p latency -20%), no regression on p50/p95 for other models, <5% cost uplift during canary. Also must have rollback path.

matt: Can we rally a 1-week spike to validate cache TTL gains in staging? I'll carve out dev time. If we get a 10-15% 95p improvement in staging, we push to canary.

dena-bot: :ballot_box_with_check: quick poll — what should be quarter-priority order?
lana: 1) Latency quick-wins (cache/scheduler)
olivia: 2) Cost optim (quant+cache reuse)
ravi: 3) Throughput infra (pool autoscale + batching redesign)

matt: fine with that order, but we should reserve a small spike for throughput feasibility research (2 engineer-weeks).

lana: Next steps: olivia to pin the metrics and customer list by EOD, matt to submit 1-week spike ticket, ravi to draft dependency risk note. We'll run a formal RICE table on Wed and lock scope. :thumbsup:

olivia: sending metrics link now: https://redwood.internal/metrics/threads/1903456789

matt: created spike ticket: PROD-3421 — 1w cache+scheduler proof-of-concept

ravi: drafting dependency note, will drop in the thread by tomorrow morning

lana: thanks team — short thread, actionable. We'll use the RICE numbers + dependency risk to finalize prioritization at Wed sync.
